column2: the plan only tightens oos language near one out-of-scope section and one “no cap” line, but `skills/shared/reviewer-templates.md` defines four independent `<!-- begin generated_body -->` blocks (code reviewer, plan fidelity, code robustness, security-structure-tests), each with its own `### out-of-scope observations` block and a separate uncapped-finding sentence (lines 237, 338, 454, 566). a partial edit would regenerate three specialist agents that still tell reviewers to report every oos item, contradicting the max-3 oos instruction and weakening the prompt-side half of the change while mechanical caps mask it downstream.

hand-maintained specialist agent files retain `no cap on the number of findings — report every issue you identify` while also gaining a 3-oos cap elsewhere. pre-rendered bodies copied from them stay contradictory, so reviewers may emit 10+ oos rows that are only dropped later at collection time.

the plan caps oos at aggregation (`plan_review_round.py`, `review_pipeline.py:collect_findings`) and updates `reviewer-templates.md` / `agents/reviewer-*.md`, but the prompts actually sent to external reviewers on `/design` and parts of `/implement` are assembled in `python/rendering.py` (`render_plan_review_main` for plan review; `_specialist_tagging` for specialist renders) and `python/review_pipeline.py` (`_dynamic_agent_body` for dynamic implement reviewers). those surfaces inline `review-acceptance-rubric.md` and allow unlimited `out_of_scope` tsv rows without referencing `oos-acceptance-rubric.md` or a per-reviewer oos cap. mechanical truncation then keeps the first three sidecar rows per slot (not necessarily the most material), can drop a high-materiality oos item if it appears fourth, wastes vendor tokens on proposals that will be discarded, and does not satisfy the issue’s explicit prompt-side proposal-instruction requirement for the design path.

the plan’s edge-case bullet requires an in-scope row after overflow oos rows, but the test bullets only require overflow suppression, dense oos numbering, and reviewer allowance. an implementation can pass those tests while breaking out after the fourth oos row or otherwise dropping later in-scope findings, regressing the collection path and making retained-row counts or `findings_count` wrong.
